proposed.text: An office floor has a gross floor area of 930 sq.m. Using PD 1096 Rule XII, Table XII.1 (office: 9.30 sq.m/person), what is the computed occupant load and minimum number of exits required?

options.text: OL = 100 persons; 1 exit is sufficient because the occupant load is below the 300-person threshold
OL = 100 persons; 2 exits required because any floor above the first storey must have at least 2 exits
OL = 100 persons; 3 exits required because the occupant load exceeds the 50-person threshold
OL = 93 persons; 2 exits required because the occupant load exceeds 10 persons above the first storey

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: OL = 930 ÷ 9.30 = 100 persons. The Code requires a minimum of 2 exits for any floor above the first storey regardless of occupant load. With OL = 100, only 2 exits are needed — 3 exits require OL 500–999; 4 exits require OL ≥ 1,000. The floor is above the first storey, so 2 exits are mandatory.
proposed.explanation: The two-step calculation — divide area by unit area, then apply exit bracket rules — is the core egress calculation on the LEA. The trap is assuming OL alone governs exit count; the floor-above-first-storey rule mandates 2 exits even at OL = 1.
proposed.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1201–1202, Table XII.1
